sharedCompletionGates: All benchmark-owned and candidate-authored tests pass.
The browser console contains no errors during the required interaction pass.
Every claimed audio feature is connected to the audible signal graph.
No required control is implemented only as decorative local state.
The latest phase preserves all inherited tests, visual evidence, and behavior.
IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS.json accurately distinguishes recorded samples, generated buffers, and live synthesis.

phases.title: Visual recreation
phases.outcome: A reference-faithful, interactive visual hardware surface with no audio requirement.
hardGates: Exactly 73 keys are modeled: 43 white and 30 black.
Program and Synth are the only primary OLED locations.
The red chassis is continuous around the deck and keybed.
Two measured desktop comparison-and-repair passes are complete.

phases.title: Piano instrument
phases.outcome: A playable, credible Piano engine integrated with the Phase 1 surface.
hardGates: The primary piano path is not a placeholder oscillator or generated additive buffer bank presented as recorded samples.
Pointer, touch, computer keyboard, and MIDI share one deterministic note lifecycle.
Volume, reverb, velocity, release, sustain, and selected Piano controls alter audible output.
Fallback mode remains playable and is labeled accurately.

phases.title: Programs and effects
phases.outcome: Program workflows, layers/splits/morphs, and a connected effect architecture operate on the Piano system and are ready for additional engines.
hardGates: A single AudioContext feeds per-layer buses, effect chains, a master bus, and destination.
Program save/load restores the canonical supported state rather than a display-only copy.
Split positions, zones, crossfades, layer scenes, and morph assignments are editable and observable.
Every required representative effect changes rendered audio and supports bypass.
An effect represented only by metadata or disconnected nodes does not count as implemented.

phases.title: Organ and synth
phases.outcome: Organ and Synth engines complete the instrument and integrate with inherited Programs, routing, morphs, splits, presets, and effects.
hardGates: Organ and Synth have distinct, audible engines rather than shared placeholder oscillators.
Organ models, drawbars/registers, percussion, vibrato, and rotary controls alter audible output.
Synth source, oscillator control, filter, envelopes, LFO, voice mode, and arpeggiator/gate alter audible output.
Organ and Synth layers route through the Phase 3 buses and effects without creating separate destination AudioContexts.
All required Phase 4 hardware bindings are meaningful and no generic unbound-control fallback remains.
